notes:
## Dial 1.0.18 — 27 Oct 2026

- **No more crashes from a menu, Dock, Finder or notification click.** A 1.0.11 Mac crashed with "panic in a function that cannot unwind": an error inside one of the places where macOS calls straight into Dial — a Dock or menu-bar pick, a Finder service, a notification click, a sleep / wake or display change, the brightness-key tap — ended the whole app, because an error may not pass back through macOS. Every one of those entry points now runs behind a guard that leaves a breadcrumb naming it in the crash report and keeps a dev build running; the kernel's sleep question is still answered when something goes wrong, a key event goes on unchanged, and the Dock menu comes back empty instead of taking Dial down. The webview also stops resizing elements from inside their own size observer (the sidebar, the status bar, the visualizer and the recorder strip), which was the source of the harmless "ResizeObserver loop" errors in the crash log.
- **Several boosted apps at once stay audible.** With a live stream, looping videos and many players all turned up to 100000 % and paused and resumed all the time, most of them went silent and only one could be heard. Dial was taking a paused player for a broken sound path, rebuilding it, upsetting the other paths while doing so, and in the end dropping the apps to their own volume — which next to apps at 1000 times is nothing. Now a pause is told apart from a path that really went dead (that one stops at the moment something changed), an app turned up past 400 % is never dropped to its own volume — a path that stays silent is kept and simply left alone for 10 s, then 30 s, then a minute — and a player that is known to pause is given 10 s before Dial does anything. The same scene was then run for three hours (the report said it took more than two): nothing grows with time any more — the waits start over after ten minutes, the lesson that a player pauses is refreshed from what it does rather than forgotten and relearned, and a busy minute no longer turns into minutes of silence for an app that really went dead. The Devices view's sound health log says "went quiet — boosted, it keeps its sound path; Dial leaves it alone for …" when that happens.
- **Boost up to 2000000 %.** With Pro (Mac and Linux), any app can now be turned up to 2000000 % (20000 times, +86 dB), twenty times the 100000 % of the day before. The popover's chevrons go 100 → 1000 → 10000 → 100000 → 2000000 % and back to 100 %; the menus, the Dock, the tray, hotkeys, links, Quick fixes and Dial AI all reach the new top, and the readouts make room for seven digits. The boost guard still keeps the sound under full scale with no clipping, and nothing in the engines can overflow at this gain — but levels like these can damage speakers and hearing, so Dial says so and asks you to turn it up slowly. Windows stays at 100 % per app.
- **Studio: face shaping you can see.** Face slimming, the V-line jaw and bigger eyes did nothing on the Mac most of the time: they only ran when a face had been found, and Dial's skin-tone finder (the Mac WebView has no face detector) often drew a box too tall or too wide to pass as a face, so the warps rested — and when they did run, a weak stretch of the whole area moved the background as much as the face. Now the skin box is made face-shaped and grown to the real face, the slimming is a smooth pinch that peaks at the cheeks and ends just outside the face (the room behind you stays put), and when no face is seen at all the effects use a centred-face guess instead of resting — the preview and the Look tab say so ("No face found — … use a centred guess").
- **Studio: the background always works.** Blur, Colour and Picture backgrounds did nothing without a found face. They now work with the centred guess too, the person mask keeps your head, shoulders and any skin near the face (hands, neck) with a soft feather, the Blur slider sets how strong the blur is (it used to half-mix a blurred picture over the sharp one, which looked like ghosting), and the background is graded together with you — a LUT, the exposure and the finish apply to both.
- **Studio: more beauty effects.** New sliders, each with its own drawn icon, a sound and a scene, and an OSC address (`/beauty/<name> <value>`): Skin warmth (cool … warm), Blush, Lip tint with a lip colour picker, Nose slimming, Chin (shorter … longer), Forehead (lower … higher); and a Finish section that works with Beauty off too: Clarity, Soft glow, Matte (lifted blacks), Dehaze, Film grain and Vignette (moved here from the Light tab). Eye brightening now lifts the eyes gently without ever pushing a bright pixel to white. The Light tab gains whole-picture Auto exposure and Auto white balance sliders beside the by-face ones. Two new LUT looks: Soft film and Vintage.
- **Studio: 19 beauty presets, each a different picture.** Natural, Soft glow, Studio light, Fresh, V-line, Bold, Soft film (soft, slightly desaturated, cool-neutral, lifted blacks, low contrast, dim soft edges, a faint glow), Golden hour, Cool film, Teal & orange, Vintage, Black & white, Glam, Clean, Bright, Night, Podcast, Gaming and Off. A preset sets every slider and its LUT look at once; your own saved presets keep their LUT; hotkeys and OSC reach all 31 slots (19 built in + 12 of your own). A slider or a preset changed from a hotkey, OSC or the Look tab reaches the preview, the recording, the stream and Dial Camera alike.

### Install

Dial is a Mac app (Apple silicon — M1 and later). One download: `Dial_<version>_aarch64.dmg`.

- **With Pour:** `curl -fsSL https://ipconfig.co.network/pour/install | sh` then `pour install --cask dial`
- **By hand:** open the DMG and drag Dial into Applications. First launch: `xattr -cr /Applications/Dial.app` (Dial is self-signed, not notarized).
- Per-app volume and the equaliser need macOS 14.4 or later.
- Earlier Windows, Linux, ChromeOS, FreeBSD and Intel Mac builds stay on the releases page but are no longer updated.
